plugin_asdk_app_69987578d8a48191b241aa0e.name: Allianz Direct España
plugin_asdk_app_69987578d8a48191b241aa0e.description:
The Allianz Direct Spain Car Insurance Explorer offers a transparent way to visualize and understand Allianz Direct car insurance options within ChatGPT. This tool helps you see how a car insurance policy could be structured, focusing on clarity and customization. Use this app to design a potential policy configuration, learn about protection details, and get an estimated price without any commitment.

Key Features:
• Detailed Coverage Analysis: Receive detailed breakdowns of what is included and what can be included in an Allianz Direct policy for a specific type of car.

• Clarified Terms: Request immediate definitions of insurance concepts (e.g., "additional coverage" or "exclusions") to ensure you fully understand the terminology used.

• Interactive Customization: Understand policy parameters, such as liability limits or specific coverage inclusions, to see how they influence the insurance estimate.

How it works:

Simply describe your car's characteristics and what you need (e.g., "A basic third-party car insurance for a Seat Ibiza"). The app will generate a corresponding non-binding policy outline. You can then ask the assistant for information about the coverage, request modifications to the details, or ask for explanations of specific clauses to see how the coverage adapts to your needs and what options are available. If you wish to proceed, the app will request the necessary details and provide a price estimate. For an official quote or policy issuance, users are directed to Allianz Direct's official purchasing channels.

Note: This tool is for informational and exploration purposes only, providing estimates based on the details shared in the chat. Official policy issuance requires verification through Allianz Direct Spain's official website. The insurance part of the Service that Allianz Direct operates is subject to human oversight by Allianz; you may contact human advisors at any time through Allianz Direct's official channels. 

Please bear in mind that AI systems may produce outputs that are inaccurate, incomplete or not fully adapted to specific circumstances, and the accuracy of any indicative quotation depends directly on the accuracy and completeness of the information provided.

Important: Do NOT provide payment data (bank account numbers, IBANs, payment card details), national identity documents (DNI/NIE), passport numbers or any other sensitive personal identification data through this chat. Such data should only be provided through Allianz Direct's secure contracting environment. 

Data required for quotation: To generate an indicative quotation, the Service will request the following information: date of birth, driving license details, vehicle data (registration plate, date of first registration and type of use), postcode, estimated annual mileage and payment frequency preference. The Service does not collect national identification documents or any special categories of personal data.

For major financial choices, use the report as a starting point and speak to a qualified professional where you need one.

Seamlessly go from quote discovery to purchase. Answer a few questions about your trip to receive a personalized CoverMe® Travel Insurance quote, then continue to CoverMe.com, where your information carries over to help make purchasing coverage quick and easy.  
Before You Get Your Quote
To generate your travel insurance quote, we'll ask for information such as your date of birth, province of residence, travel destination, travel dates, and trip cost. Manulife uses the information received through this plugin to generate your quote, assess eligibility, and support the travel insurance quote and purchase process. Please provide only the information requested, and do not share additional information unless specifically requested as part of the quote process.
This plugin is available through ChatGPT, which is provided by OpenAI and is subject to OpenAI's terms, privacy practices, account settings, and data-handling practices.
This tool is intended only to help you request a travel insurance quote. It cannot be used to submit or manage a claim, request emergency or travel assistance, or send urgent or time-sensitive communications to Manulife. It supports single-trip coverage for one traveller. If you have pre-existing medical conditions, are looking for multi-trip or group coverage, or are not a Canadian citizen or resident, this tool may not be suitable for your needs. Do not use this tool to provide detailed medical information, health histories, treatment information, or other sensitive personal information. If you provide information about other individuals, please make sure you have their permission to do so.  
This experience helps you obtain a travel insurance quote and does not provide professional insurance advice. 
The quote provided is for informational purposes only and is not an insurance contract or guarantee of coverage.
For more information about how your information is collected, used, and protected, please review our Canadian Privacy Policy and Legal Information & Disclosures.

plugin_asdk_app_6a2a589865a88191933e9bad.description:
Exercise now or wait. Sell at vest or hold. Which lots to sell first. Each of these has a right answer for your specific situation, and it turns on how alternative minimum tax (AMT), holding periods, state tax, and the time value of taxes paid early interact across several years. That is where rules of thumb break down. Ask in plain language and OptionsAhoy returns the answer with the year-by-year schedule behind it.

1. Which incentive stock options (ISOs) to exercise in which year, to hold down AMT and recover the credit later. We optimize across multiple years, with your tax status in mind.

2. Whether to sell restricted stock units (RSUs) at vest or hold for long-term capital gains, and what the twelve-month cliff is actually worth. We show you the optimal solution.

3. Which vested RSU lots to sell and in what order, and what that saves against selling oldest-first (the default order your broker's UI will offer). This sounds like a minute optimization. On a $725,000 sale from a concentrated position, the gap between the optimal order and your broker's default could be over $100,000 in tax.

4. Whether non-qualified stock options (NSOs) are better exercised and sold, or exercised and held.

5. Whether your shares pass the six statutory tests for qualified small business stock (QSBS). Best to check early for potential tax savings, the rules just changed.

6. How exposed a single position leaves you, and what selling down, holding, or hedging each cost. We calculate and compare different strategies across three years, with your taxes in mind.

7. What a protective put or a zero-cost collar prices at. If you need to protect your holdings, you're probably considering a hedge. But which one? We make it easy to decide.

8. How to convert some of your holdings to a target amount of after-tax cash by a deadline with the smallest tax bill. We optimize against your inputs and risk tolerance, then you choose, the way an investment firm would.

Every result is computed against the federal tax code plus all fifty states and the District of Columbia. The 2026 federal constants match IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-32. Federal cases reproduce to the cent against the independently maintained PSL Tax-Calculator, and state results reproduce to the cent against OpenTaxSolver across California, New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, and Massachusetts. That proof recomputes live in your browser at optionsahoy.com/verification.

This matters because language models are confident and wrong at exactly this task. In a published benchmark, five frontier models were given the same multi-year ISO problem, three runs each. All five overstated the after-tax value of their own proposed schedules, by 1.6x to 17.6x against the provable optimum. One model claimed $3.9M, $5.2M, and $13.0M on three runs of identical input. The prompt and full transcripts are public at optionsahoy.com/benchmark. The arithmetic here is deterministic instead: the same inputs on the same date give the same answer every time, with no model inference anywhere in the number.

Free, no account, no API key, and your figures are not retained. United States tax logic only. This is a planning calculator, not tax advice.

plugin_asdk_app_6a75db4073348191b50fd065.description:
O OnePro conecta sua conta ETF1 ao ChatGPT e dá acesso à mesma base de dados e
aos mesmos motores de análise que você usa na plataforma.

Consulta de ativos: fichas completas de ETFs brasileiros e globais, ações, BDRs,
FIIs, fundos CVM, debêntures, renda fixa pública e privada e índices,  custos,
patrimônio líquido, retornos históricos, alocação e composição. Screener com
filtros por classe, look-through da carteira de ETFs (inclusive ETFs de ETFs) e
lookup reverso ("quais ETFs carregam NVDA?").

Análise de carteira: seus portfólios salvos no OnePro, ou uma carteira informada
na conversa, avaliados por retorno, volatilidade, Sharpe, Sortino, drawdown
máximo, tempo de recuperação e correlação, contra benchmarks como CDI, IBOV,
IFIX, IMA-B e S&P 500. Inclui ranking entre carteiras, consistência em janelas
móveis de 10 anos e heatmap de CAGR real por ano inicial.

Motores de simulação: fronteira eficiente e carteira de máximo Sharpe;
probabilidade de atingir uma meta de patrimônio (goal-based investing); projeção
prospectiva de patrimônio por Monte Carlo; e plano de retirada da aposentadoria
com taxa segura (SWR), taxa perpétua (PWR) e estratégias clássico,
rebalanceado, bucket e dynamic spending com guardrails.

Todos os resultados vêm de um snapshot diário de dados, com a versão do dado
declarada em cada resposta, e os motores raciocinam em termos reais (R$ de hoje e dólar).
O conector é somente leitura: nenhuma operação altera dados da sua conta, e
nenhuma ordem de compra ou venda é executada. As análises são informativas e não
constituem recomendação de investimento.

Requer assinatura ativa do OnePro em etf1.com.br.

plugin_asdk_app_6a8f6d7d50d081918787990d.description:
RoboSystems turns public-company financial filings into a knowledge graph ChatGPT can query directly.

SEC EDGAR: every public company's XBRL filings as one queryable graph. Pull a company's financial statements by ticker or CIK, pivot reported facts across companies, periods and dimensions, resolve a concept like "revenue" to its XBRL element, and run full-text search across filing narratives, then read the exact section.

Read a filing the way it was filed: list the statements and notes in a 10-K or 10-Q, then open one section whole, with its rows, breakdowns and the calculations that tie it together.

The graph also exposes read-only Cypher, so a conversation can move from a question ("show me NVIDIA's latest income statement") to a raw traversal ("which 2025 10-Ks mention goodwill impairment?") without leaving ChatGPT.

Authorization is OAuth 2.1 with PKCE. This plugin connects only to the SEC EDGAR repository, which is read-only, and you can revoke access at any time. Open source (Apache-2.0): github.com/RoboFinSystems/robosystems

Built for portfolio managers, research analysts, index providers, and allocators who need defensible, data-driven answers to thematic questions.

plugin_asdk_app_6aa9789071f4819194e9d6b3.name: Bizora Tax Research
plugin_asdk_app_6aa9789071f4819194e9d6b3.description:
Bizora is an AI native tax research platform. This connector brings Bizora’s research engine into ChatGPT, so you can ask a tax question in the middle of your actual work and get an answer grounded in primary source authority rather than secondary commentary.

Ask the question the way you would ask a colleague. Bizora interprets it, researches it against the governing authority, and returns a reasoned answer with citations you can open and verify yourself. Responses point back to the sources that control the issue, including the Internal Revenue Code, Treasury regulations, revenue rulings and revenue procedures, IRS guidance, and federal case law. State and international authority is included where the question calls for it.

Common uses:

- Researching a client position before you commit to it on a return
- Checking whether recent legislation or guidance changes an answer you already relied on
- Working through cross-border and multistate questions where the authority is scattered
- Building the technical support behind a memo, a client email, or a workpaper
- Getting oriented on an issue outside your usual specialty

Because the connector runs inside ChatGPT, the research sits alongside the rest of your work. You can pull up a client email, research the question it raises, and draft the reply in one thread.

Every tool in this connector is read only. Bizora retrieves and analyzes tax authority without creating, modifying, or deleting your client records or research source material. Research usage is metered against your Bizora account credit balance.

Bizora is a research tool, not a substitute for professional judgment. Review the cited authority before relying on any answer in client work.

plugin_asdk_app_6abc4e34f1a8819191694205.description:
Distill Markets gives ChatGPT direct access to US SEC filing data, served exactly as filed and traceable to the EDGAR accession that stated each number.

What it covers:
- Fundamentals from 10-K and 10-Q XBRL: latest values, up to 20 years of history, financial ratios, and a bring-your-own-price valuation panel.
- Point-in-time views: what was knowable on a past date, every version of a fact across filings, and material revisions, for restatement-aware research and backtests without lookahead.
- Ownership: 13F institutional holders and manager portfolios, Schedule 13D/13G blockholders, and Form 4 insider transactions.
- Filings and events: recent SEC filings, 8-K item events, and a delta feed for agent loops.
- Context: 16 government macro series and sector capital-cycle aggregates.
- Pre-2009 annual fundamentals parsed from text filings (FY1995 to FY2009), kept separate from the XBRL record and served with per-fact provenance.

Every tool is read-only. Responses carry the accession number, filing date and XBRL concept behind each value, so any figure can be checked against the SEC document. The server states no opinions and gives no investment advice: it reports what the filer said and how it reconciles.

Coverage is US domestic 10-K and 10-Q filers. Figures are in the filer's reporting currency, never converted.

A free account covers most tools. Analyst and Pro plans add depth: full ownership lists, point-in-time detail, cross-ticker comparison and the pre-2009 corpus.

plugin_asdk_app_6aa583fd0db081919ad974b7.name: חשמלינק
plugin_asdk_app_6aa583fd0db081919ad974b7.description:
Chashmalink answers questions about Israeli household electricity from measured smart-meter data rather than estimates off a bill.

Behind it sits an analysed corpus of more than 20,000 Israeli households across 500+ municipalities, each a full hourly export from Israel Electric Corporation — up to 17,520 meter readings per home. That is what lets these tools answer with a number rather than a rule of thumb.

Ten read-only tools:

• compare_electricity_plans — rank every plan on the Israeli market by what it would save a specific household, per month and per year. Takes a monthly kWh figure or, far better, a 24-hour load curve.

• simulate_solar_tracks — price Israel's two mutually exclusive rooftop solar tracks against a real load shape, with payback and a recommendation. Which one pays more depends on WHEN a household consumes — the thing a roof-area calculator cannot see.

• get_city_consumption_benchmark — median monthly consumption, profile mix and 24-hour curve for a given Israeli city.

• get_national_load_curve — national demand by hour, day of week and season.

• classify_consumption_profile — classify a home as evening, night, morning, weekend or balanced, with peakiness and a night-shift opportunity figure.

• estimate_appliance_cost, size_air_conditioner, compare_ev_running_cost — running costs for appliances, air conditioning and electric cars at the current tariff.

• get_supplier_directory — every supplier and plan with its discount structure.

• how_to_export_my_iec_data — how a household downloads its own consumption file.

Privacy: no per-household data is reachable here. Every figure is either computed from the caller's own inputs or is a population aggregate published only where at least 25 analysed households sit behind it; a thinner cohort is refused rather than answered thinly. Nothing here writes, submits or contacts anyone.

Free, no account, no API key. Figures are in shekels and kWh.

plugin_asdk_app_6a65fc65294c8191b3066182.name: DREAMHALL
plugin_asdk_app_6a65fc65294c8191b3066182.description:
You already have a life. Build the one you want.

DREAMHALL is a private, structured self-care workspace for thinking through personal questions whose answers should remain your own. Instead of generating conclusions, it guides you through a complete process where you examine your life as a whole, develop your own answers, and turn them into grounded decisions and practical action.

The Framework consists of 15 connected exercises that help you understand what truly matters to you, review the balance of your life, separate your own wishes from outside expectations, clarify the future you want to build, work through fears and obstacles, and define realistic next steps.

Unlike an open-ended conversation, DREAMHALL is designed as a finite process with a clear beginning, a deliberate sequence, and a meaningful ending. Every answer is written by you. Every conclusion is your own. The result is a Personal Document that brings together your reflections, priorities, decisions, and next steps in one place.

Your private answers remain inside DREAMHALL and are not returned to ChatGPT through this integration.

When you finish, you can keep your Personal Document in DREAMHALL, download it as a PDF, or export it as Markdown. If you choose, you can later use your own document with ChatGPT to organize ideas, develop plans, compare future versions, or expand it into longer writing. You decide what to share and when.

DREAMHALL supports reflective thinking, life balance, personal wellbeing, and self-directed decision-making. It is a non-clinical self-care product and is not therapy, diagnosis, medical care, emergency support, or crisis support.

Some of the most important decisions should remain your own.

Developers use SmartSpectra rPPG for remote vital signs monitoring, telehealth intake, contactless health checks, employee wellness screening, driver fatigue detection, clinical trial screening, and digital biomarker collection across iOS, Android, and web.

The SmartSpectra SDK is built by Presage Technologies, who in 2026 received FDA 510(k) clearance (K254169) for heart rate and breathing rate in its SmartSpectra Vital Signs Monitor 1.0. Presage serves healthcare, government, and wellness markets from Leesburg, Virginia, USA.

plugin_asdk_app_69528c304ff0819186557905.name: trainedby.ai
plugin_asdk_app_69528c304ff0819186557905.description:
trainedby.ai connects your wearables to ChatGPT, so your AI coach knows your real training load, sleep patterns, and recovery without you typing a word.

**The problem with AI fitness coaching today**

People are turning to ChatGPT to plan their marathon training, strength programs, or HYROX prep. It makes sense, because AI is available 24/7, extremely patient, and quite knowledgeable.

But somehow it doesn't quite work.

And that is because you have to tell it everything. Every. Single. Time.

Every conversation starts from zero. You have to describe in detail your current level, recent workouts, schedule, and goals. You paste in screenshots from Garmin. You try to remember what you did last week, how you slept, that your resting HR has been elevated, or that your HRV has been trending down for weeks.

The advice is based on what you told it, not what actually happened.

And what you tell it is incomplete, subjective, and often wrong.

What if your AI coach could see everything?

We connect your wearables (Garmin, Oura, Whoop, Apple Health, and 50+ other platforms) directly to your AI assistant.

When you open ChatGPT and ask about your training, it already knows:
- Workouts from the past weeks, months, and year
- Sleep quality and patterns
- Heart rate variability and resting heart rate trends
- Daily activity and recovery metrics
- Nutrition and menstrual cycle data (if you track it)

No more context dumps. No more subjective self-reporting.

**How it works**

We use smart compression to turn weeks of wearable data into something an AI can understand and analyze. Instead of dumping raw heart rate readings into a chat window, we surface the trends and patterns that matter—elevated resting HR, declining HRV, increasing training load, poor sleep consistency.

The data rolls up from days to weeks to months to years, so you can spot trends.

And because it's integrated into ChatGPT, you just start chatting.

Beyond wearable data, you can add notes like workout goals, feedback, and other personal information such as availability and injuries. This way, the AI gets that bit of subjective context it needs to give you the best advice.

**Who this is for**

If you're already wearing a watch or ring, and using AI to help plan your training, whether that's for a marathon, strength program, or general fitness, trainedby.ai makes that experience dramatically better.

**Get started**

The product is free to use.

Connect your wearables, add the integration to your AI assistant, and start chatting.

plugin_asdk_app_6a57f362b92481919c078e43.legacyDescriptionSource:
BurnWeek is an AI calorie tracker that meets you where you already are. Just say what you ate - "a flat white and a chocolate croissant," "chicken burrito bowl" - and BurnWeek estimates the calories and protein for you and adds it to your day. Because food is never exact, BurnWeek shows honest ranges (e.g. "680-780 cal") instead of fake-precise numbers.
Ask how your day is going and BurnWeek shows what you've eaten and how much you have left. BurnWeek also tracks a 7-day sliding-window budget, so one big day doesn't mean failure - you just balance it out over the week. Made a mistake? Say "undo that." Got the portion wrong? "Make the rice 200 grams" and the estimate recomputes. You can also save recipes and favorites, set up recurring meals, log from a photo or a barcode, and plan meals ahead.
BurnWeek logs to your own private account. Connect your existing BurnWeek app history with a one-time link code so your meals stay in sync between the app and ChatGPT. BurnWeek is general-wellness software, not medical advice, and it never collects payment, location, or health-record data.

plugin_asdk_app_6a561b226d8c8191a8deba84.description:
Trabber is a travel metasearch engine. Search for a flight, a place to stay or a rental car, and you get the current prices from the airline, travel agency, hotel and car rental websites that sell it, side by side, plus a direct link to book the one you pick on that seller's own website.

Why that helps: the identical trip can cost quite different amounts depending on where you buy it, and the cheapest seller changes from one route or property to the next. Checking by hand means a dozen browser tabs. Here you ask once.

What you can search:

- Flights, one way, return or multi-city.

- Accommodation of any kind: hotels, apartments, aparthotels, hostels, guest houses, villas, campgrounds.

- Rental cars.

- Flight deals, for when you have no destination or dates in mind yet.

Narrow any search down by asking: direct flights only, morning departures, breakfast and free cancellation, automatic with unlimited mileage. Connect your Trabber account and you can pick your recent searches back up.

Trabber doesn't sell travel. You book, pay and get support on the seller's website, under their terms.

plugin_asdk_app_6a7857ebf7c48191938b9913.name: Vize Rehberim
plugin_asdk_app_6a7857ebf7c48191938b9913.description:
An information and calculation tool for visa applications by citizens of Türkiye (ordinary/burgundy passport).

It answers questions like "Do I need a visa for Japan?", "How much does a German visa cost?" and "How many Schengen days do I have left?" — always with its source.

What it covers:

· Visa status for 172 countries — 55 visa-free, 23 visa on arrival, 30 e-visa, 64 requiring a consulate application
· Per country: the fee, the published processing time, the application centre and the required documents
· Refusal rates for Schengen applications made from Türkiye, based on European Commission statistics (27 countries)
· Appealing a refusal: the competent authority, deadline, language and fee for seven Schengen countries, and the meaning of all 17 refusal grounds on the standard form
· Calculators: the Schengen 90/180 day allowance, multiple-entry (cascade) eligibility, and the total cost in Turkish lira at the central bank rate

How the data is collected:

Every amount and duration is verified against an official consulate, ministry or legislative source, quoted verbatim. A value that cannot be verified is not published — nothing is estimated; the field is left empty and said to be empty. Answers carry their source and last-updated date.

Only the consulate of the country concerned can grant a visa. We are not an agency: we do not file applications, book appointments, or guarantee approval.

BookYolo is an AI-powered travel tool designed to help you inspect the quality of hotels and vacation rentals before you book them. The platform analyzes public listing information and guest feedback to surface fatal flaws,  hidden red flags, review patterns, overselling and marketing techniques, fee surprises and expectation gaps that travelers often miss. BookYolo goes beyond ratings and surface level reviews by running a deep analysis of each property through a 100-point inspection.

plugin_asdk_app_69c28d6aedac81919502a88c.description:
Play chess without leaving ChatGPT. Start a new game in seconds, make moves in normal chess language, and talk about every part of the game as you play. You can ask why a move is good, why a move is bad, what to do next, or how to get better. This app is made for people who want to play, learn, and have fun at the same time.

The app is easy to use. Just begin a game and make your moves. You can use simple move names, standard chess notation, or ask questions in plain English. If you are not sure what to do, ask for help. The game keeps going while you chat, so learning feels natural instead of like reading a long lesson.

If you are brand new to chess, this app is a friendly place to start. It explains ideas in small, simple steps. It tells you what each piece can do and why some moves are stronger than others. You never have to pretend you understand. Just ask another question. You can learn one move at a time.

If you already know how to play, you can go deeper. Talk about openings, middle games, endgames, tactics, strategy, planning, and common mistakes. Ask why a position feels better for one side. Compare different moves. Explore new ideas. The conversation changes to fit your questions.

Play at your own speed. Think for a long time or move quickly. Stop to ask about a position. Go back and look at an earlier move. Try a different idea and see what could happen. Chess is not only about finding the best move. It is also about understanding why that move works.

The app can explain forks, pins, skewers, discovered attacks, double checks, sacrifices, passed pawns, king safety, piece activity, space, time, and many other chess ideas using clear language. Hard topics become easier because you can ask for another explanation whenever you need one.

Want to improve? Review your games after they finish. Talk about turning points, missed chances, and strong moves. Ask where the game changed. Find patterns in your play. Learn from mistakes instead of simply seeing that they happened. Every game becomes a chance to get stronger.

You can also practice specific parts of chess. Focus on openings you want to remember. Study endgames that appear often. Learn how to attack, defend, trade pieces, or make better plans. Ask for tips that match your current skill level instead of getting the same advice every player receives.

The conversation is just as important as the game. Ask “What if I move here?” Ask “What was my best move?” Ask “Why did my attack fail?” Ask “Can you explain that in a simpler way?” The app is built for questions, so you are never limited to playing in silence.

There is no need to switch between different tools just to play and learn. The chessboard and the conversation work together. You make a move, ask a question, get an answer, and keep playing. Everything happens in one place, making practice smooth and enjoyable.

Whether you play one game a week or many games every day, the app is ready. Beginners can build confidence. Casual players can have fun. Club players can explore ideas. Anyone who enjoys chess can have interesting conversations while playing.

Use the app to play complete games, test new ideas, understand difficult positions, review finished games, and discover better moves. Learn at your own pace. Stay curious. Ask as many questions as you like. Every move is another chance to think, learn, and enjoy the game. If you want a chess game that also talks with you, teaches you, and helps you improve inside ChatGPT, this app is ready to play.

plugin_asdk_app_6a72d5743ab481918bff8de4.description:
Play Texas Hold’em poker with an AI opponent, then talk about every hand with ChatGPT. This is more than a poker game. It is a place to play, learn, ask questions, and get better one hand at a time. If you are new to poker, the AI can help you understand what is happening. If you already know the game, you can test ideas, try new plans, and review your choices. Every game becomes a chance to learn.

You can sit down and start playing in just a few moments. The game follows the rules of Texas Hold’em. Cards are dealt, bets are made, and each hand plays out like a real game. When the hand ends, you can ask ChatGPT why something happened. Ask why a bet was good, why a fold was smart, or why a bluff worked. You can keep asking until it makes sense.

Learning poker does not have to feel hard. Big ideas are explained with small, simple words. If you do not know what a flop, turn, river, or blind is, just ask. If you want to know what pot odds mean, ask. If you want help reading the board or choosing between calling, raising, or folding, ask. The AI explains each step in a clear and friendly way.

You are free to play the way you want. Try safe play. Try bold play. Bluff more. Bluff less. See what happens. If something goes well, ask why. If something goes wrong, ask what you could do next time. Every choice is a chance to learn something new.

This is not only for beginners. Players with more experience can explore strategy, compare ideas, and think through tough spots. Magic Tips turns "when should we go?" into a concrete answer.

Ask for a resort and a month, and you get a daily crowd score from 1 to 10

weather data and seasonal events, then normalised against each park's own
demand range.

• Attraction catalogues per park — minimum height, ride duration, must-do
  flag and community rating

  Lane, DAS, rope drop), available in 13 languages

not include live wait times or ride closures. Crowd scores are forecasts,
not guarantees; the methodology and its known limits are published at
https://magic-tips.app/en/methodology

Magic Tips is an independent, fan-made project. It is not affiliated with,
endorsed by, sponsored by, or officially connected to The Walt Disney
Company or any of its subsidiaries or affiliates. Park, attraction and
character names are trademarks of their respective owners and are used
here only to identify the places this tool covers.

plugin_asdk_app_69adad9bda08819187d81b71.description:
Everything your favorite kitchen management app does, and more, inside ChatGPT.

Pantry Persona remembers what's in your fridge, what your family can and can't eat, and which brands you prefer. It stores your recipes, plans your meals, builds your shopping lists, and tracks the nutrition behind it all, then keeps everything in sync as you cook and shop through the week

**Recipes** — Save a recipe from a website, a cooking video, or a social post, or just create one in conversation. Search by ingredient, cuisine, or what you can make right now with what's on hand, and group your favorites into collections.

**Meal plans** — Generate a full week of meals in one ask, or build it day by day. Plans respect your household's food preferences and eating rules automatically, and carry per-meal nutrition so you can see how the week shapes up.

**Shopping lists** — Visual, interactive lists organized by store. One tap checks items off. Ask for a shopping list from your meal plan and it skips anything already in your pantry. Send it to Instacart when you're ready to buy.

**Cook Mode** — Start cooking a recipe and get step-by-step guidance. When you're done, ingredients are deducted from your pantry and leftovers are tracked with expiration dates.

**Nutrition** —  See calories and macros on every recipe and meal, set your own daily targets for each person, and check how today or the week is stacking up. Log what you actually ate, even a meal out, and it counts toward your totals.

**Your kitchen, personalized** — Household profiles store each family member's food preferences, eating rules, favorite brands, and nutrition targets. Every suggestion, plan, and search filters through them so you don't have to repeat yourself. Invite other family members and everyone works from the same pantry, recipes, and shopping lists in real time.

Also tracks pantry expiration dates, predicts when you'll run low on staples, learns the brands and prices you buy, and turns grocery receipts into an up-to-date inventory and a clear picture of your spending.

plugin_asdk_app_6a451d5c44f881919c7b0c75.description:
Play drums without leaving the chat. Tap the drum kit, make a beat, and let ChatGPT listen to what you played. It can tell you what went well, where you stayed on time, where you rushed or slowed down, and simple ways to get better. You do not need special gear or music skills to start. Open the app, play, and get feedback in the same conversation.

The drum kit lives right inside ChatGPT, so there is nothing extra to learn before you begin. Every hit is captured as you play. ChatGPT can look at your rhythm, timing, speed, and patterns instead of guessing from a description. That means the advice is based on what you actually played, not what you tried to explain. You can ask questions after every take, try again, and see how your playing changes over time.

This makes practice simple. Play a slow rock beat. Try a fast fill. Make up your own groove. Copy a rhythm you heard in a song. Then ask ChatGPT what it noticed. It can point out steady parts, missed beats, uneven spacing, and places where your hands could work together better. If something sounds good, it can explain why. If something feels hard, it can break the problem into small steps.

Beginners can use it to learn basic beats and build confidence. More experienced drummers can test ideas, explore different rhythms, or check how consistent their timing is. Teachers can use it to help students understand practice sessions. Parents can give children a fun way to explore music without needing a full drum set at home. Anyone who is curious about rhythm can jump in and start playing.

Because everything happens in one conversation, practice feels natural. You play, ChatGPT listens, you ask questions, and you get answers right away. There is no need to switch between different apps, upload recordings, or explain what happened. The performance is already there for ChatGPT to review. That keeps the focus on making music instead of managing files.

You can ask for different kinds of feedback too. Want a quick score? Ask for one. Want a detailed breakdown? Ask for that instead. Want tips that are easy enough for a child to follow? ChatGPT can do that. Want advice that feels more like a drum teacher? It can change its style to match your goals. You control the conversation.

The app is also great for small challenges. See if you can keep a steady beat for one minute. Try playing softer or louder. Practice using only one hand. Build a simple groove and slowly make it more interesting. After each try, ChatGPT can explain what changed and suggest the next challenge. Little wins add up, and every new rhythm gives you something to learn from.

This creates a different kind of music experience inside ChatGPT. Instead of only talking about drumming, you can actually drum. Instead of getting general advice, you receive feedback tied to your own performance. Instead of stopping to move between tools, everything stays together in one place. The result is a playful way to practice, learn, experiment, and improve. Whether you have never held a pair of sticks, already play every week, or just want to tap out a fun beat for a few minutes, the app turns a conversation into an interactive practice space where every hit can become a chance to learn.

plugin_asdk_app_6a30d2fd05c88191adc78db2.legacySummary: 民事法律帮助，覆盖 50 州
plugin_asdk_app_6a30d2fd05c88191adc78db2.description:
Courtroom5 serves self-represented litigants (SRLs) — people who must navigate civil court without an attorney, typically because they cannot afford one. Roughly 80% of civil litigants in the United States appear without legal representation. Without guidance, they lose cases on procedural technicalities before the merits are ever heard.

The Courtroom5 app gives ChatGPT users access to three jurisdiction-aware legal tools: a case intake assessment that evaluates a user's situation and identifies applicable civil claims; a deadline calculator that returns precise procedural deadlines and consequences by state and court level; and next-step guidance for users already in active litigation. All tools are scoped to civil matters in US state and federal courts and designed for plain-language delivery to non-lawyers.

Courtroom5 is a Techstars graduate and recipient of the ABA Woman of Legal Tech recognition. We have served over 12,000 self-represented litigants across all 50 states.

plugin_asdk_app_6a0c3f3f51e88191851fe363.name: Who What Wear
plugin_asdk_app_6a0c3f3f51e88191851fe363.description:
Who What Wear brings the women's fashion publication's editorial voice into ChatGPT. It works like having a stylist who already knows your taste — once you've set up a short style profile, every fashion question gets a personalised, brand-aware answer instead of a generic one.

Setup takes about a minute. A guided four-step widget asks for your style words (Low-Key Luxury, Tailored, French, Sporty, Trend-Forward and others), the brands you actually shop across contemporary, luxury, denim and accessories, the style icons whose looks you'd happily borrow, and the price range you're comfortable with. The profile is saved per user, so it carries across conversations rather than starting over every time you open ChatGPT.

After onboarding, three things become useful.

Shopping for a specific item. Tell the app what you're looking for — "find me a black blazer under £250", "I need a coat for a winter wedding", "what jeans should I buy" — and it returns three to five picks weighted toward the brands you already buy from, plus a complete outfit built around the piece: what to wear on top, on the bottom, on your feet, and one or two accessories. The aim is to leave with a wearable answer, not a list of links.

Editorial inspiration. Ask what you should be wearing or looking at right now, and the app pulls fresh articles from Who What Wear UK's live editorial feed, then picks the two or three that match your taste using the brand and category tags on each article. The picks render as a horizontal carousel of cards in the publication's own visual language: editorial image, kicker, headline, byline credit, and a link straight back to the article on whowhatwear.com.

Refining your profile. Taste shifts. Reopen the onboarding to update any answer (and only the answers you want to change), or reset the profile entirely if you're starting fresh.

A few things worth knowing. The editorial feed is Who What Wear UK, so the content leans British in voice, currency and seasonality. Recommendations are always anchored in real Who What Wear articles or in brand suggestions drawn from the list you provided — the app does not invent URLs, images, or articles to fill out a result, and the carousel only renders when there are real links and images to attach. If the feed has nothing relevant on a given day, you get an honest reply rather than a fabricated one.

What the app is not: it does not cover men's fashion, beauty product search, home decor, or non-fashion shopping. It does not surface live retailer inventory or live prices. If a request falls outside this scope, it says so instead of guessing.

Built by Future PLC, publisher of Who What Wear.

plugin_asdk_app_69619eb270748191a34b2ac1.name: Tonita
plugin_asdk_app_69619eb270748191a34b2ac1.description:
Tonita is a search engine for apparel and accessories, built to work with how you actually think about shopping. It brings together products from hundreds of stores, thousands of brands, and millions of items — all in one place, from clothing and footwear to cosmetics and everyday essentials.

There isn’t just one way to shop. Sometimes you’re focused on price or practicality; other times it’s about style, fit, materials, or longevity. What matters can shift with the situation — work, travel, special occasions, outdoor use, or everyday wear. Tonita brings these options together, making it easier for you to browse, compare, and make an informed choice.

Within ChatGPT, Tonita works best as part of a conversation. You can explore broad questions, half-formed ideas, or specific constraints naturally — whether that means thinking through what to buy for a particular occasion, learning about materials or categories, or narrowing in on a specific kind of product. ChatGPT helps shape your thoughts into useful searches, and Tonita surfaces a wide set of relevant results for you to browse, compare, and refine as the picture becomes clearer. (For more advanced tools like virtual try-on, saving favorites, and deeper browsing, Tonita can also be used directly at Tonita.co.)

Tonita is built to support the way you actually think about shopping — by priorities, context, and tradeoffs — rather than forcing everything into rigid categories. This includes the ability to search and explore across aspects like:

• Budget and value: From fast fashion and sale finds to higher-end pieces, investment items, and everyday staples.
• Style and aesthetic: Minimalist, maximalist, classic, streetwear, formal, playful, utilitarian, fashion-forward, or timeless — and combinations of these.
• Trends and longevity: What’s popular right now, last season’s styles, and pieces meant to stay relevant beyond a trend cycle.
• Use case and setting: Work, travel, special occasions, outdoor use, events, lounging, or everyday wear.
• Fit, sizing, and comfort: Different body types and needs, including petite and extended sizing, relaxed or tailored fits, and comfort-first designs.
• Materials and feel: Natural fibers, synthetics, performance fabrics, lightweight layers, structured pieces, or materials chosen for warmth, breathability, or softness.
• Durability and care: Easy-care basics, machine-washable items, wrinkle-resistant pieces, or garments meant to be worn, repaired, and kept longer.
• Sustainability priorities: Interest in materials, production methods, longevity, or brands taking different approaches to environmental impact.
• Brand familiarity and discovery: Well-known labels alongside emerging brands, niche designers, and alternatives to the usual options.
• Putting a full look together: Apparel, footwear, accessories, jewelry, and cosmetics, considered side by side rather than in isolation.

Agnic Gifts buys one real, physical gift and ships it — inside the conversation you are already having.

Tell ChatGPT who the gift is for and what you want to spend. It searches vetted shops in the US, UK, Canada and Australia and comes back with real items that are in stock, within budget and shippable to your address, not links to go and read later.

Pick your own: see the candidates named and priced, ask about any of them — delivery cost, materials, size, whether it is still in stock — and choose the one you want.

Your card never enters the conversation: it is held in a PCI DSS certified vault and the model never sees a number.

Agnic never holds your money. The shop is the seller, the shop ships the order, and returns and refunds go through the shop under its own policy.

Physical goods only, one gift at a time, and any gift that has not been bought yet can be cancelled.

Paste a LinkedIn post and see which rhetorical formulas readers have seen too often.

The plugin counts a small set of formulas and compares each count with a reference corpus of published LinkedIn posts in the same language. For every formula, it reports the value found, how the post compares with the reference posts and, when a formula is used more than usual, a concrete suggestion to say the same thing more directly.

French and English, and it says which one it measured. French carries three formulas: the "ce n'est pas X, c'est Y" contrast, three lines in a row opening on the same word, and the announced lesson ("Résultat :"). English carries one, the "it's not X, it's Y" contrast: the other two were measured on English posts and were not reliable, so they are left out.

It is a style check only. It does not rewrite the post, and it does not assess who wrote it or how it was produced. No account needed.

plugin_asdk_app_6a9f12de5b508191b0798371.name: LetsPackUp
plugin_asdk_app_6a9f12de5b508191b0798371.description:
Plan a trip with the assistant you already talk to, and it turns into a real trip in LetsPackUp: organized, and ready to share with the people you are travelling with.

Ask for a week in Portugal with three friends, and the assistant lays it out in LetsPackUp the way a trip should be laid out. Days in order, with times. Every stop on the map. A packing list. A place to note who paid for what, so the money is fair without anyone doing the sums. Then you share it, and it is one trip for everyone, not a chat thread of screenshots.

What your friends and family see when you share it
- The plan, day by day, with the times and the places.
- Every stop on a map, with notes for each one.
- The packing list, so nobody forgets the charger.
- Who paid what and who owes whom, worked out for the group.
- A calendar to find the dates everyone can make.
- A group chat and polls to settle the open questions.
- An idea box where anyone can propose an afternoon, a restaurant or a whole day, and the group votes.

Everyone you invite opens the same trip on the web or on Android, and it works without a connection once it is loaded. Whatever anyone adds, the whole group sees.

How the assistant fits in
The assistant works only in the trips you choose and does only what you allow: looking at the plan, adding to it, creating trips, or also deleting things, reading the chat, posting to it, and creating share links for trips you own. You decide once, you can change your mind at any time, and you can switch the assistant off with one click. Everything it adds appears under your name, and the group can edit it, vote on it or take it out.

What stays yours
The assistant never changes what your co-travellers wrote. It never sees their email addresses, their location, their files or their emergency contacts, and it never sees where anyone actually is. It cannot remove anyone from a trip, and it cannot delete a trip you created yourself.

LetsPackUp is free, and so is using it with your assistant. It works in 16 languages. Questions: https://letspackup.com/en/faq or support@letspackup.com.
